# Progress

A bar that reports how far along something is. Built on Radix Progress, so the value is announced to assistive tech for free. The label and readout are droppable parts, a chrome variant strips the track, and a duration makes it a self-running countdown.

```tsx
<Progress value={64} />
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add progress
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/progress/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

Pass `value` (0 to `max`, which defaults to 100). That alone renders the bare bar. Anything you pass as children becomes the row above it, so a label and a readout are composed in rather than switched on: there is no `showLabel` prop, and dropping either part simply removes it.

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/ui/progress"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Progress value={72}>
      <ProgressLabel>Importing components</ProgressLabel>
      <ProgressValue />
    </Progress>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/ui/progress"

<Progress value={…}>
  <ProgressLabel />
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

## With a label and a readout

`ProgressValue` prints a whole percentage by default and reads the value from context, so it never drifts from the bar. Give it a function to phrase the readout yourself: `{(value, max) => …}` receives the same numbers. It is `aria-hidden`, because Radix already exposes the value on the bar itself and a screen reader should not hear it twice.

```tsx
<Progress value={72}>
  <ProgressLabel>Importing components</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

## Sizes

Four heights. `xs` (4px) is page chrome: the reading or loading bar pinned under a header. `sm` is the default for a bar sitting in content, `md` and `lg` for a bar that is the point of the panel it is in.

```tsx
<Progress value={58} size="xs" />
<Progress value={58} size="sm" />
<Progress value={58} size="md" />
<Progress value={58} size="lg" />
```

## Tones

The fill takes any of the semantic roles, so a bar can report health as well as distance: flip to `success` when a task lands, `destructive` when a quota is nearly spent. Every tone is a token, so all four themes track it.

```tsx
<Progress value={64} tone="brand" />
<Progress value={100} tone="success" />
<Progress value={48} tone="warning" />
<Progress value={22} tone="destructive" />
<Progress value={76} tone="info" />
<Progress value={40} tone="foreground" />
```

## Vertical

`orientation="vertical"` stands the bar up for the things that fill from the floor: a tank, a level meter, a quota per volume. The fill rises from the bottom, `size` sets the bar’s width instead of its height, and the header parts stack centred above it, so `ProgressLabel` still names the bar. The bar is as tall as the root: give it a height with `className` (it is 128px otherwise), or let its parent size it, a column flex parent included: `h-auto flex-1` takes what the column leaves. The semantics do not change: the root is still a Radix progressbar reading the value, and it carries `data-orientation` as a styling hook. There is no `aria-orientation`, since ARIA does not allow it on a progressbar.

```tsx
<Progress orientation="vertical" size="lg" value={40} tone="success" className="h-40">
  <ProgressLabel>Tank 3</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

For a tank gauge rather than a line, restyle the track through its `data-slot`: it fills the root’s width and becomes a ringed well, and padding on it insets the fill, which rises as a share of the well’s inner height (no `calc()` to write). Step the radii down concentrically: a 24px well with an 8px inset holds a 16px fill. The fill takes the track’s corners, so without the inset a low level in a round-cornered track is carved by the track’s own outline; the inset keeps it a clean pill at any height. Here each gauge is a flex item of a column, taking whatever height the column leaves it. The fill and the indeterminate sweep work the same at any width.

```tsx
// The gauge flexes into its column: no height on the Progress itself.
<div className="flex h-64 w-24 min-w-0 flex-col items-center gap-2">
  <Progress
    orientation="vertical"
    value={64}
    tone="success"
    aria-label="Unleaded tank"
    className="h-auto w-full flex-1 [&_[data-slot=progress-indicator]]:rounded-lg [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:w-full [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:rounded-2xl [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:bg-[var(--surface,var(--background))] [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:p-2 [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:ring-1 [&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:ring-border"
  >
    <ProgressValue />
  </Progress>
  <span className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground">Unleaded</span>
</div>
```

## On a muted ground

The track is a relative tint of the foreground rather than the opaque muted token, so it always sits one step off whatever is behind it: on a card it reads as the muted groove it always was, and on a muted ground (a selected table row, a muted panel) it still shows, where a muted groove would vanish into the row. Nothing to set: it is how the track paints.

```tsx
// The selected row paints bg-muted, as a selected DataTable row does.
<li data-selected className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4 rounded-lg px-3 py-2.5 data-selected:bg-muted">
  <span>Vitals</span>
  <Progress value={60} aria-label="Vitals: 60% done" className="w-24" />
</li>
```

## A running task

Between discrete steps the fill glides rather than snapping, so a jump from 24% to 36% reads as movement. Start the upload to watch it climb and land on `tone="success"`.

```tsx
<Progress value={value} tone={done ? "success" : "brand"}>
  <ProgressLabel>{done ? "Upload complete" : "Uploading assets"}</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue>{(v) => `${Math.round((v / 100) * 24)} of 24 files`}</ProgressValue>
</Progress>
```

## Indeterminate

Pass `value={null}` when there is no percentage to report. The fill becomes a short pill sweeping the track, which says "working" without inventing a number, and the readout falls back to a dash. Radix drops the value from the accessibility tree too, so the bar is announced as indeterminate rather than as zero.

```tsx
<Progress value={null}>
  <ProgressLabel>Connecting to the registry</ProgressLabel>
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

## Timed

Pass `duration` (in ms) instead of a value and the bar runs itself: the countdown on an alert that closes on its own, a cooldown, the fill of a [Hold Button](https://www.koalaui.com/docs/components/hold-button.md). `onComplete` fires when the time is up. The fill is the full bar slid along the track on `transform`, a CSS animation on the compositor, so nothing re-renders and nothing is laid out while it runs, and the leading end keeps its round cap all the way. `paused` freezes it where it stands and resuming carries on with the time that was left; a new `runKey` starts it again from the top. Here the alert closes after 8 seconds unless the pointer or focus is on it.

```tsx
<Alert variant="warning" className="overflow-hidden" onPointerEnter={hold} onPointerLeave={release}>
  <Progress
    duration={8000}
    runKey={raised}
    paused={hovered || focused}
    onComplete={close}
    variant="chrome"
    size="xs"
    tone="warning"
    aria-label="Time until this alert closes"
    className="absolute inset-x-0 top-0"
  />
  <AlertIcon />
  <AlertContent>
    <AlertTitle>10-31 · Robbery in progress</AlertTitle>
    <AlertDescription>Fleeca Bank, Vinewood Blvd. Closes in 8s; hover to hold it.</AlertDescription>
  </AlertContent>
</Alert>
```

`direction="drain"` (the default) empties a full bar, the time running out; `"fill"` fills an empty one, the time building up. Changing `duration` or `direction` restarts the run as well. A timed bar reports no value to assistive tech, because a number that moves without re-rendering would be stale the moment it was read: give it a name and, where the time matters, say it in words beside the bar. Under reduced motion it ticks about once a second instead of gliding. The root carries `data-timed`, `data-paused` while paused and `data-complete` once it has run out.

```tsx
<Progress duration={4000} runKey={run} paused={paused} onComplete={…}>
  <ProgressLabel>Drain · cooldown</ProgressLabel>
</Progress>
<Progress duration={4000} direction="fill" tone="success" runKey={run} paused={paused} onComplete={…}>
  <ProgressLabel>Fill · charging</ProgressLabel>
</Progress>
```

## Reading progress

`useScrollProgress()` returns how far the document has been scrolled, 0 to 100. Feed it to a `chrome` bar and you get the reading indicator that rides under a navbar: no track, square ends, and `transition="none"` so the fill is welded to the scrollbar. A transition here would trail the page by 300ms and read as lag, not polish. Pass it a ref to follow a scroll container instead (a reader pane, a modal body), which is what the panel below does. The [blog post page](https://www.koalaui.com/marketing/pages/blog-post.md) ships the document version.

```tsx
const progress = useScrollProgress()        // the document
// const progress = useScrollProgress(paneRef) // or a scroll container

<Progress
  value={progress}
  variant="chrome"
  size="xs"
  transition="none"
  aria-label="Reading progress"
  className="sticky top-0 z-30"
/>
```

## API reference

### Progress

The bar, `role="progressbar"`, over Radix `Progress.Root`; forwards its props but `asChild`. Children become the row above the track. Every part accepts `className`, merged last.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| null | 0 | 0 to `max`, clamped. `null` is indeterminate: the fill sweeps. |
| max | number | 100 | The top of the scale, so `value={3} max={8}` is a step counter. |
| size | "xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | "sm" | Track thickness: 4, 6, 8 or 12px (its width when vertical). |
| tone | "brand" \| "foreground" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "destructive" \| "info" | "brand" | The fill's colour. |
| variant | "default" \| "chrome" | "default" | `chrome` drops the track and squares the ends, for a full-bleed reading or loading bar. |
| transition | "smooth" \| "none" | "smooth" | `smooth` glides between steps; `none` welds the fill to a per-frame value like scroll position. |
| orientation | "horizontal" \| "vertical" | "horizontal" | `vertical` fills from the floor; give the root a height (128px by default). |
| aria-label | string | - | Names the bar when there is no `ProgressLabel`. |
| duration | number | - | Timed mode, in ms: the bar runs itself over this long and `value` is ignored. |
| direction | "drain" \| "fill" | "drain" | Timed mode: empties from full, or fills from empty. |
| paused | boolean | false | Timed mode: holds the bar where it is. |
| runKey | React.Key | - | Timed mode: change it to restart the run. |
| onComplete | () => void | - | Timed mode: called when the run reaches its end. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-state | `loading`, `complete`, or `indeterminate` while `value` is `null` (set by Radix). |
| data-value | The clamped value (set by Radix). |
| data-max | The `max` (set by Radix). |
| data-orientation | `horizontal` or `vertical`. |
| data-timed / data-paused / data-complete | Present in timed mode, while paused, and once the run has ended. |

| CSS variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| --progress-track | The track's ink: a 4% foreground tint (6% in dark), so it reads on any ground. Override per instance. |

### ProgressLabel

What is progressing. Names the bar through `aria-labelledby` unless the root has its own label. Renders a `<span>`.

### ProgressValue

The readout, a whole percentage by default, `aria-hidden` since the bar already announces it. Renders a `<span>`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | (value: number \| null, max: number) => React.ReactNode | - | Phrases the readout yourself, e.g. `3 of 8`. `value` is `null` while indeterminate. |

### useScrollProgress

`useScrollProgress(ref?)` returns how far the document (or the referenced container) is scrolled, 0 to 100. Pair it with `transition="none"`.

## FAQ

### Why is the label a part instead of a prop?

So it can be dropped. Every part of a Koala component is omittable and composed rather than switched on with a `showX` flag: `<Progress value={64} />` is the bare bar, and adding `ProgressLabel` or `ProgressValue` as children builds the row above it. That also means you can put anything else in that row - a file count, a cancel button, a tone chip.

### Do I need to announce the value myself?

No. The root is a Radix Progress, so it already carries `role="progressbar"` with the value, min, and max. Give it an `aria-label` (or point `aria-labelledby` at your own heading) when the bar has no visible label. `ProgressValue` is `aria-hidden` on purpose, so the number is not read out twice.

### When should the fill animate, and when should it not?

`transition="smooth"` (the default) glides between discrete steps: an upload going 0 → 33 → 66 looks like progress rather than a series of jumps. `transition="none"` is for a value that changes every frame, like scroll position - a 300ms transition chasing a per-frame value always trails behind and reads as lag. Both honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### What does the chrome variant change?

It drops the muted track and squares off the ends. A bar that spans the full viewport has no edges to round and no gutter to sit a track in, so the fill paints straight onto the page. It is the treatment for a reading bar or a top-of-page loading bar; a bar sitting in content should stay on the default.

### Can I use a scale other than 0-100?

Yes. Pass `max` and the value is read against it, so `value={3} max={8}` is a step counter. The default readout still prints a percentage; pass a function to `ProgressValue` to phrase it as "3 of 8" instead.

### How do I make a vertical bar?

Pass `orientation="vertical"` and give the root a height (`className="h-40"`, 128px by default), or let a parent size it: inside a column flex parent, `className="h-auto flex-1"`. The fill rises from the bottom, `size` sets the bar's width, and `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` stack above it. For a wide gauge, widen the track with `[&_[data-slot=progress-track]]:w-full` on the root.

### Why does the track stay visible on a selected table row?

It paints a relative tint of the foreground (4% in the light themes, 6% in the dark ones, the Tabs pill track's ink) instead of the opaque muted token. On a card that lands on the muted groove; on a muted ground it still sits one step darker (or lighter, in dark), so the bar never loses its track.

### Why width instead of a transform?

Scaling a rounded bar squashes its pill caps into ellipses at low values, which is visible on the larger sizes. The fill is a single element inside a fixed-height, overflow-hidden track, so animating width costs nothing measurable and keeps the ends honest. A timed bar is the exception: it animates every frame for seconds at a time, so there the full-length fill slides on `transform` instead, which keeps the caps round and stays on the compositor.

### How do I count down without re-rendering every frame?

Pass `duration`. The bar runs itself as a CSS animation and a timer beside it fires `onComplete`, so React renders it once per run, not once per frame. Pause it with `paused` (hover and focus on a toast-like card, a game menu opening) and restart it with a new `runKey`.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add progress` writes `components/ui/progress/`. Import from `@/components/ui/progress`:

- Components and helpers: `Progress`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue`, `progressVariants`, `useScrollProgress`
- Types: `ProgressProps`, `ProgressLabelProps`, `ProgressValueProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `radix-ui`
